1. Model consistently overestimates prices in the short term, especially after recent spikes or high values — adjust forecast downward by 2–5% for the next 3–5 days post-spike.

2. Model underestimates prices during sharp downward trends — increase forecast by 3–7% when true outcome drops below 30% of historical mean over 30-day window.

3. Model exhibits mean reversion bias — if forecast is above 45% of 30-day moving average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.

4. Forecast lags true price movements by 1–3 days — adjust for lag by adding 1–2% to forecast for each day of delay in true price reversal.

5. Overshoot after spikes — if model forecast exceeds true outcome by >10% for 2+ consecutive days, reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 3 days to avoid overcorrection.

6. Model ignores volatility clustering — if true outcome shows 3+ consecutive days of volatility >10% from prior day, increase forecast variance by 1–2% to reflect higher uncertainty.
